title: Leo · Living the ordinary days
orientation: Twelve linked moments about daily life after Eva’s death. Use the prompted skill, give feedback and retry. Each next scene is a new moment, not a response to your exact words.

scenes.bridge: An ordinary morning brings mixed feelings.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the peace and guilt together.
scenes.text: [Half-smile] Breakfast is peaceful now. I hate that I can like the quiet.
scenes.suggestion: The quiet gives you a little peace, and liking it brings guilt alongside that.

scenes.bridge: Leo wonders what relief says about his love.
scenes.prompt: Explain exploration without making a moral verdict.
scenes.text: [Careful] If I feel the relief properly, won’t that make me a worse husband?
scenes.suggestion: Exploring relief doesn’t decide what kind of husband you were. It may help distinguish wanting rest from not loving Eva.

scenes.bridge: In another moment, he distinguishes Eva from the hospital demands.
scenes.prompt: Validate the distinction without erasing the love.
scenes.text: [Self-critical] I miss her, but not the endless waiting at the hospital. I shouldn’t separate those.
scenes.suggestion: You can miss Eva and not miss the strain of those visits. They aren’t the same thing.

scenes.bridge: Relief and guilt are not yet easy to separate.
scenes.prompt: Ask one question that clarifies the relief.
scenes.text: [Quietly] The relief and guilt seem tangled.
scenes.suggestion: If we take the relief first, what were you relieved from?

scenes.bridge: Saying he was exhausted brings a small ease and self-judgment.
scenes.prompt: Make room for the ease before the judgment takes over.
scenes.text: [Hesitant] Saying I was exhausted brings ease, then a voice calling me selfish.
scenes.suggestion: Could we hear the ease first, before that judgment takes all the room?

scenes.bridge: Leo describes the care through its schedule.
scenes.prompt: Tentatively check what is harder to share.
scenes.text: [Quietly] I can explain the hospital schedule. The tiredness is harder to say.
scenes.suggestion: Maybe the schedule feels safer to share than how much it cost you. Is that close?

scenes.bridge: He uses a practical phrase for life after caregiving.
scenes.prompt: Bring the experience closer using his phrase, with room to disagree.
scenes.text: [Flatly] I’m off duty now. Strange phrase for your wife, but there it is.
scenes.suggestion: The watch has ended, while being her husband hasn’t simply ended inside you. Is that close?

scenes.bridge: A wish for rest gives way to listing appointments.
scenes.prompt: Check whether he wants to return to that wish.
scenes.text: [Voice softens, then lists] I wanted rest. The appointments were Monday, Wednesday, sometimes Friday—
scenes.suggestion: The schedule shows the demands. Would you like to pause with wanting rest before we list more?

scenes.bridge: Leo is emotional and asks for a bounded pause.
scenes.prompt: Respect the pause without assuming he wants to end.
scenes.text: [Voice catches] I need a pause, not to finish for the day.
scenes.suggestion: A pause. We can slow down and check what you want after it.

scenes.bridge: In another moment, an enjoyable walk brings fear of leaving Eva out.
scenes.prompt: Hear the enjoyment and its difficult meaning.
scenes.text: [Quietly] Tom’s jokes helped. Then I felt I’d left Eva out of the afternoon.
scenes.suggestion: Enjoying Tom’s company felt good, then seemed to put your connection with Eva at risk.

scenes.bridge: Leo names a small change in how enjoyment can belong.
scenes.prompt: Explore what shifted without promising it will last.
scenes.text: [Quietly] Enjoying the workshop needn’t mean leaving Eva out. That feels new.
scenes.suggestion: What has helped enjoyment and your connection with her fit alongside each other?

scenes.bridge: Time is short, and the work is still unfinished.
scenes.prompt: End the hour without claiming resolution.
scenes.text: [Tearful, watchful] I’m okay to leave, but don’t call this resolved.
scenes.suggestion: It isn’t resolved. We’re ending the hour, and can note what you want to return to.
